findings.title: Good-domain Inquisitor explanation text emits the literal string "{magnitude}" instead of the number
findings.evidence: In ground_or_block_inquisitor_domain_power, `power_specific` for the GOOD_DOMAIN_SELECTION branch is a plain &str literal — "The +{magnitude} bonus is applied to her own baseline melee attack bonus..." — that is never itself passed through format!(). It is only later interpolated as `{power_specific}` into the OUTER format! call at line 15968. Rust does not re-parse already-substituted text for further `{}` placeholders, so the emitted explanation detail literally contains the seven characters `{magnitude}` rather than the computed bonus value. The sibling `value: magnitude` field on the same ComputationExplanation is unaffected (still numerically correct), but the human-readable detail text — the thing this whole file exists to keep trustworthy per its own 'grounded explanation' doctrine — is wrong for every Inquisitor who selects the Good domain and activates Touch of Good.
findings.fix_description: Either move the `{magnitude}` substitution into a real format!() call producing `power_specific` (passing `magnitude` as a named arg), or restructure so the Good-domain sentence is written as its own format! with `magnitude` bound, then interpolated as a fully-resolved String.
findings.risk_notes: src/rules_core/pilot_compute/mod.rs is compiled and exercised by `cargo test` at repo root, which scripts/verify.sh runs — per the ground rules this file's fixes must stay report_only regardless of triviality.

findings.title: 18 near-identical `is_supported_<class>_single_class` gate functions collapsible into one table-driven check
findings.evidence: has_supported_class_chassis (line 13118) ORs together is_supported_uc_single_class, is_supported_cavalier_single_class, is_supported_alchemist_single_class, is_supported_inquisitor_single_class, is_supported_oracle_single_class, is_supported_brawler_single_class, is_supported_hunter_single_class, is_supported_arcanist_single_class, is_supported_warpriest_single_class, is_supported_slayer_single_class, is_supported_swashbuckler_single_class, is_supported_investigator_single_class, is_supported_shaman_single_class, is_supported_witch_single_class, is_supported_summoner_single_class, is_supported_bloodrager_single_class, is_supported_skald_single_class, is_supported_pu_single_class (18 of 18 examined in this chunk). Every one of the 13 ACG/APG-exact-match variants has the identical body shape: destructure `[class_level]`, compare `XxxClassId::from_class_id_str(...) != Some(XxxClassId::Y)`, then call `<book>::class_chassis_resolve(XxxClassId::Y, class_level.level, RuleSetId::Xxx).is_some()` — differing only in the enum variant, book module, and RuleSetId constant.
findings.fix_description: Replace the 13 exact-match gates with one data table of (ClassFamily enum, book module fn pointer, RuleSetId) rows plus a single generic `is_supported_exact_match_single_class(input, table)` walker; keep is_supported_uc_single_class/is_supported_pu_single_class/is_supported_generic_single_class as-is since their doc comments explain a deliberately different (broad vs. exact) admission policy.
findings.risk_notes: Several of this file's own doc comments explicitly defend keeping per-class functions separate ('parallel-copy discipline', reviewability per class) — a collapse should preserve the exact per-class doc citations as table row comments, not just delete them. File is exercised by scripts/verify.sh's cargo test, so report_only regardless.

findings.title: Inquisitor Justice/Protection/Purity judgment: 3 identical-shape formula fns + 3 identical-shape 'active' query fns
findings.evidence: inquisitor_justice_judgment_attack_bonus, inquisitor_protection_judgment_ac_bonus, and inquisitor_purity_judgment_save_bonus (lines ~15307/15315/15323) all share the exact body `1 + i16::from(level) / 5`. active_inquisitor_justice_judgment_bonus (15372), active_inquisitor_protection_judgment_bonus (15408), and active_inquisitor_purity_judgment_bonus (15444) are byte-for-byte identical control flow (find Inquisitor level -> check choice_selection against one SELECTION_ID const -> find the activation -> check EquippedActive -> check rounds_consumed_today budget -> return Some((level, formula(level)))), differing only in which SELECTION_ID constant and which formula function is called.
findings.fix_description: Collapse the 3 formula fns into one `inquisitor_judgment_bonus(level: u8) -> i16` (the formula is identical for all three) and the 3 active-query fns into one `active_inquisitor_judgment_bonus(input, selection_id: &str) -> Option<(u8, i16)>` parametrized by the selection id.
findings.risk_notes: None of the three uses actually differ in formula (all `1 + level/5`), so this is lower-risk than PC3-2's collapse; still report_only per the verify.sh exclusion.

findings.title: Misleading indentation in ground_alchemist_bomb_and_poison_resistance's if/else — match body reads as top-level code
findings.evidence: The `} else {` at line 14649 opens a block whose body (the `match alchemist_poison_resistance_bonus(level) { ... }` spanning lines 14650-14687) is indented at the SAME level as the `else {` itself, rather than one level deeper — so on a quick read the match block looks like it sits outside the else-branch at the function's top level instead of inside it. The logic is correct (the match genuinely is the else-branch body, confirmed by brace counting), only the formatting is wrong.
findings.fix_description: Re-indent lines 14650-14687 one level deeper to match normal rustfmt output.
findings.risk_notes: Cosmetic only; no behavior change. Presumably rustfmt was not run after this hunk was hand-edited.

findings.title: Natural submodule-extraction seam: the ACG/APG per-class grounding clusters (Cavalier/Alchemist/Inquisitor/Oracle/Witch/Summoner/Arcanist) are self-contained but inline in this 78.5k-line file
findings.evidence: compute_apg_class_chassis (13897) dispatches to per-class clusters that are each internally self-contained (their own consts, formula fns, active_/ground_/unmet_ helper fns, and a single push_<class>_other_features_deferred_diagnostic) and reference only shared primitives (choice_selection, ComputationExplanation/Diagnostic, ability_modifier helpers) plus that class's own rules_tables/*::class_chassis_resolve and corpus lookup modules (alchemist_spell_list, witch_spell_list, domain_power, archetype_resolver). The Alchemist cluster alone (roughly lines 14396-15290, ~900 lines) has zero call-in from the Inquisitor, Oracle, Witch, or Summoner clusters and vice versa.
findings.fix_description: Extract each class cluster into its own file (e.g. pilot_compute/apg_alchemist.rs, apg_inquisitor.rs, apg_oracle.rs, apg_witch.rs, apg_summoner.rs, apg_arcanist.rs, apg_cavalier.rs) re-exported via `pub(crate) use` from mod.rs, following the existing pattern already used for rules_tables submodules (apg::, acg::, uc::, pu::). This chunk alone (12128-19600, ~7.5k lines) is about 10% of the whole 78.5k-line file and is almost entirely one clean seam.
findings.risk_notes: Purely organizational; would need care to keep #[cfg(test)] modules and any cross-cluster shared consts (e.g. ORACLE_MYSTERY_POOL used only within Oracle's own cluster) correctly scoped. Out of this lane's write scope regardless.

findings.title: Production `.expect()` couples two independently-defined lookup functions in a different module
findings.evidence: `resolve_metamagic_feat_effect(&feat_name).expect("evaluate_metamagic_feat_prerequisites already confirmed eligibility")` assumes that if evaluate_metamagic_feat_prerequisites(feat_name).is_eligible is true, resolve_metamagic_feat_effect(feat_name) is guaranteed Some. Checked against src/rules_core/feat_prereqs/metamagic.rs: both currently iterate feat_tables() with the identical predicate `entry.category == FeatCategory::Metamagic && matches_feat_id(entry, feat_id)` (one via .any(), one via .find()), so today the invariant genuinely holds and this cannot panic. But the two functions are separately maintained (no shared assertion, no test pinning that they must stay in lockstep), so a future edit to either one's filter (e.g. adding a PREREQ check to one but not the other) would silently reintroduce a live panic on a legitimate, previously-working character.
findings.fix_description: Either derive one function from the other (e.g. have resolve_metamagic_feat_effect call evaluate_metamagic_feat_prerequisites internally, or vice versa) so they cannot structurally diverge, or replace the .expect() with a claim-blocking diagnostic push + early return, matching this file's own everywhere-else discipline of never letting external-shaped data panic a production path.
findings.risk_notes: Not a live bug today (verified the two predicates are byte-identical); flagged as a latent hazard given this codebase's own stated no-panic-on-real-input discipline.
